text: True or False: Topological protection in photonics is absolute, so a protected edge mode is immune to material absorption and fabrication-induced frequency shifts just as it is immune to backscattering.
explanation: False. Topological protection is bounded and specific: it suppresses backscattering into certain channels but does nothing against material absorption or fabrication-induced frequency shifts. The chapter insists that 'topologically protected' must always be completed by the clause 'against which disorder', because robust is not the same as perfect.
